fields.headline:
3.3
Inclined Plane FBDs
fields.subhead: Tilt the axes and split the weight into parts along and into the slope.

imageSubjects.section: a wooden ramp leaning against a loading dock in low light

fields.headline: Tilt the Axes on a Slope
fields.subhead: The angle between W and the tilted y-axis equals the ramp angle.
fields.a1_b: x along the slope, y perpendicular to the slope.
fields.a2_b: mg sin(angle), pointing down the slope.
fields.a3_b: mg cos(angle), pressing into the surface.

fields.headline: Normal Force Is Not the Weight
fields.subhead: The steeper the ramp, the less the surface pushes back.
fields.c1_b:
N gets close to mg.
Almost nothing pulls
the block along.
fields.c2_b:
N gets close to 0.
The pull along the
slope nears mg.
fields.mustwrite: On an incline, N = mg cos(angle), not mg.

fields.headline: Block on a 30° Ramp
fields.subhead: Frictionless. Tilt your axes before you calculate anything.
fields.problem: A 5.0 kg block sits on a 30° ramp. Draw its FBD. Find both weight components and N.
fields.q2_b:
along: mg sin(angle)
into: mg cos(angle)
fields.answer: Along: 24.5 N  ·  Into: 42.4 N  ·  N = 42.4 N

fields.headline: Net Force Along the Slope
fields.subhead: Frictionless. The push is parallel to the ramp.
fields.problem: A worker pushes a 12 kg crate up a 25° ramp with 30 N. Find the net force along the ramp.
fields.q1_b:
m = 12 kg, angle = 25°
push = 30 N up the ramp
